A worker pool over a channel

The inner braces matter: the MutexGuard is dropped before f(j).await, so the workers actually run in parallel instead of serialising on the receiver lock.

Limit concurrency without a semaphore

This is the single most useful line in async Rust. buffer_unordered keeps throughput high without opening 10,000 sockets.

Rate limit to N per second

For a distributed limit, use governor (token bucket, correct under contention) or a Redis counter with an expiry.

Fan out, then collect in order

join_all returns in order; FuturesUnordered returns as they complete. Choose deliberately — most bugs here are a mistaken assumption about which one you used.

Timeout one step, not the whole pipeline

Debounce rapid events

Share state across tasks

Trap: let g = self.inner.read().await; held across an .await blocks every writer for the duration of unrelated work. Copy what you need, drop the guard.

Cancel a task properly

abort() is not instant: the task is cancelled at its next .await. Anything that must not be interrupted belongs in a separate task or a transaction.

Parallel CPU work inside an async service

One blocked worker thread starves every task scheduled on it. spawn_blocking uses a separate, growable pool sized for exactly this.
